Start streaming the first two episodes on @DisneyPlus TONIGHT at 9PM PT.|archivedate=20220527025509}} |last aired=[[June 22]], 2022{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-june-2022|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in June 2022}} |creators= |writers=*[[Joby Harold]]{{SW|url=news/obi-wan-kenobi-series-cast|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Series to Begin Production in April, Cast Revealed}} *[[Hossein Amini]]{{WebCite|url=https://directories.wga.org/project/1221058/obi-wan-kenobi|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi|work=[[Wikipedia:Writers Guild of America West|Writers Guild of America West]]|date=2022-02-28|archivedate=20220420023729}} *[[Stuart Beattie]] *[[Andrew Stanton]] *[[Hannah Friedman]] |directors=[[Deborah Chow]]{{SW|url=news/deborah-chow-obi-wan-kenobi-series|text=Deborah Chow to Direct Obi-Wan Kenobi Series Exclusively on Disney+}} |executive producers=*[[Kathleen Kennedy]] *[[Michelle Rejwan]] *Deborah Chow *[[Ewan McGregor]] *Joby Harold |production company= |starring=Ewan McGregor |music=*[[Natalie Holt]]{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/04/obi-wan-kenobi-composer-natalie-holt-john-williams|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi Composer Natalie Holt Reveals "Haunting" Approach|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-04-22|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220422150613}} *[[William Ross]]End credits of "Obi-Wan Kenobi" *[[Peter Nickals]] *[[Jon Opstad]] *[[Max Aruj]] *[[John Williams]] {{C|Primary motif only}} |timeline=[[9 BBY]]{{KenobiDate|I}} }} {{Quote|Between darkness and defeat, hope survives.|Teaser trailer| }} '''''Obi-Wan Kenobi''''', marketed as '''''Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi''''', is a live-action television miniseries developed by [[Lucasfilm]]. It premiered on [[Disney+]] on [[May 26]], [[2022]] and concluded on [[June 22]], 2022. The series features [[Ewan McGregor]] and [[Hayden Christensen]] reprising their roles from the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]], respectively [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. It takes place ten years after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and nine years before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. ==Official description== ''During the reign of the Galactic Empire, former Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi embarks on a crucial mission. Kenobi must confront allies turned enemies and face the wrath of the Empire.''{{DisneyPlus|url=series/obi-wan-kenobi/2JYKcHv9fRJb|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi}} ==Development== ===As a film=== {{Quote|It wasn't always going to be a series, not initially. When we first started talking about, that wasn't really in the cards, but everything's changed so much, so quickly. It's really exciting that it is now. I'm really into the idea to be able to tell the story over several hours instead of just one hit. I think it's going to be quite cool.|Ewan McGregor on how the series evolved from a film|{{WebCite|url=https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/1107165-kenobi-was-originally-going-to-be-a-solo-film|text=Exclusive: Ewan McGregor Confirms Kenobi Was Originally One Film|author=Sabina Graves|date=2019-10-27|work=[https://www.comingsoon.net comingsoon.net]|archivedate=20200613111757}}}} [[File:Obi-Wan_Kenobi_EP1.png|thumb|left|175px|Ewan McGregor first appeared as Obi-Wan Kenobi in [[1999]].]] In [[2013]], news was released that [[The Walt Disney Company]]-[[Lucasfilm]] brand was developing several theatrical pictures separate from the [[Star Wars saga|core, episodic]] ''[[Star Wars]]'' saga, which were later denominated as the ''[[Star Wars Anthology Series]]'' line.{{SW|url=news/new-spinoff-films-set-to-expand-the-star-wars-galaxy|text=New Spinoff Films Set to Expand the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy}} Talks about a potential Obi-Wan Kenobi-centric movie as part of the Anthology series arose, and [[Ewan McGregor]], the actor who played Kenobi in the ''Star Wars'' [[prequel trilogy]], was approached to reprise the role. However, McGregor knew about the project as far back as [[2015]],{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/obi-wan-kenobi-mcgregor-kept-series-secret-longer|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi: McGregor Kept the Series a Secret Longer Than You Think|author=Samuel Gelman|date=2019-10-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Comic Book Resources|''Comic Book Resources'']]|archivedate=20200107023840}} and until [[2019]], he was forced to withhold information in interviews.{{WebCite|url=https://www.mensjournal.com/features/ewan-mcgregor-cover-story|text=Ewan McGregor Is Back on Top—Again|author=Mickey Rapkin|date=2019-10-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Men's Journal|''Men's Journal'']]|archivedate=20200727012231}} ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', the first installment of the Anthology Series, was released in [[December]] [[2016]] and was well received both critically and commercially.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/star-wars-spinoffs-on-hold|text=Exclusive: Future 'A Star Wars Story' Spinoffs on Hold at Lucasfilm|author=Steve Weintraub|date=2018-06-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20200810070905}} In [[August]] [[2017]], sources from [[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']] reported that an Anthology film centered on Obi-Wan Kenobi starring McGregor was in development by Lucasfilm, with [[Wikipedia:Billy Elliot|''Billy Elliot'']] director [[Stephen Daldry]] in early talks to direct and oversee the project.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/obi-wan-kenobi-star-wars-film-planned-director-talks-1030505|text='Star Wars' Obi-Wan Kenobi Film in the Works (Exclusive)|author=Borys Kit|date=2017-08-17|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200805044822}} [[Joel Edgerton]], who portrayed [[Owen Lars]] in the prequel trilogy, had previously expressed interest on reprising his role in a spin-off film about Kenobi.{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/joel-edgerton-uncle-owen-obi-wan-star-wars-movie|text=Joel Edgerton Wants to Reprise Uncle Owen in the Obi-Wan Movie|author=Amanda Hayman|date=2018-06-08|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|''Screen Rant'']]|archivedate=20190209031837}} Once he was hired to helm the film, Daldry contacted [[Hossein Amini]] to talk about the possibility of joining the project.{{WebCite|url=https://discussingfilm.net/2019/11/07/hossein-amini-talks-the-success-of-the-alienist-approaching-the-screenplay-for-drive-his-upcoming-disney-obi-wan-series-exclusive-intervi|text=Hossein Amini Talks The Success Of 'The Alienist', Approaching The Screenplay For 'Drive' & His Upcoming Disney+ 'Obi-Wan' Series (Exclusive Interview)|author=Jacob Fisher|date=2019-11-07|work=[https://discussingfilm.net discussingfilm.net]|archivedate=20200423170910}} However, all ''Star Wars'' stand-alone spin-off films were put on hold following the lower-than-expected box office returns from ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', the second Anthology film, in [[May]] [[2018]]. [[September|Four months later]], Disney [[Wikipedia:Chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Bob Iger (chief executive officer)|Bob Iger]] revealed that Lucasfilm had reevaluated its release schedule in the wake of the poor reception of ''Solo''.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/bob-iger-disneys-streaming-service-james-gunn-star-wars-slowdown-1145493|text=Bob Iger Talks Disney's Streaming Service, 'Roseanne,' James Gunn and a Coming 'Star Wars' "Slowdown"|author=Matthew Belloni|date=2018-09-20|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200511001454}} It was later confirmed that there will be a hiatus on ''Star Wars'' following the release of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']] until [[2022]].{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-avatar-star-wars-marvel-1203207661|text=Disney Moves 'Avatar' Sequels, Announces New 'Star Wars' Films|author=Brent Lang|date=2019-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200727083136}} Despite this, former UK Foreign Secretary [[Wikipedia:Boris Johnson|Boris Johnson]] was quoted in [[November]] 2018 as saying that the filmmakers of the Obi-Wan Kenobi film had proposed shooting it in Northern Ireland.{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/starwars/amp/news/uk-foreign-secretary-claims-george-lucas-to-shoot-obi-wan-spinoff|text=Former UK Foreign Secretary Claims George Lucas Plans to Shoot Star Wars Spinoff Obi-Wan Kenobi Movie|author=Jamie Jirak|date=2018-11-24|work=[[Wikipedia:ComicBook.com|''ComicBook.com'']]|archivedate=20200815222217}} ''The Hollywood Reporter'' had previously voted it in a 2016 poll as the most wanted Anthology film by fans.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/star-wars-darth-vader-spinoff-movie-should-happen-923065|text=Darth Vader Deserves a 'Star Wars' Spinoff (But Not Everyone Agrees)|author=Graeme McMillan|date=2016-08-26|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20191028203330}} ===As a series=== {{Quote|I want to get closer and closer to how Obi-Wan felt while Alec Guinness was playing him. I feel like I'm grayer and nearer him in age, so it'll be easier to do that.|Ewan McGregor on playing Obi-Wan in the series|}} [[Stuart Beattie]] was hired by Lucasfilm to write a script for the Obi-Wan movie.{{WebCite|url=https://thedirect.com/article/obi-wan-kenobi-movie-trilogy-before-disney-exclusive|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi Movie Trilogy Was Planned Before Disney+ (Exclusive)|author=Nathan Johnson|date=2022-06-27|work=[https://thedirect.com The Direct]|archivedate=20220701174100}} McGregor then participated in a costume test for the planned film.{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/ewan-mcgregor-donned-obi-wan-kenobis-costume-on-the-set-of-the-mandalorian|text=Ewan McGregor donned Obi-Wan Kenobi's costume on the set of The Mandalorian|author=Alyssa Mercante|date=2020-10-27|work=[[Wikipedia:GamesRadar+|''GamesRadar+'']]|archivedate=20201027114511}} However, at some point in development, the film project turned into a television series instead. Beattie's script—the first of a planned trilogy—served as the basis for the the series, which was officially announced by McGregor and Lucasfilm President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] at the 2019 [[Wikipedia:D23 (Disney)|D23 Expo]] after months of rumors and speculation. It takes place ten years after [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. During the event, it was also revealed that the episodes had already been written and that production would begin in [[2020]].{{SW|url=news/d23-expo-2019-8-things-we-learned-about-star-wars-at-the-disney-showcase|text=D23 Expo 2019: 8 Things We Learned About ''Star Wars'' at the Disney+ Showcase}} Amini and [[Deborah Chow]] were later announced as showrunners in [[StarWars.com]]. Reva, the chief villain of the series, was originally killed off in Beattie's script.{{WebCite|url=https://thedirect.com/article/obi-wan-kenobi-reva-killed-script-exclusive|text='Obi-Wan Kenobi' Killed Off Reva In Original Script (Exclusive)|author=Nathan Johnson|date=2022-06-28|work=[https://thedirect.com The Direct]|archivedate=20220701031102}} On [[January 23]], 2020, it was reported that the series had been put on hold due to alleged "script problems."{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/obi-wan-series-delayed-disney-plus|text=Exclusive: 'Obi-Wan' Disney+ Series on Hold as Crew Sent Home|author=Adam Chitwood|date=2020-01-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20200714102135}} However, McGregor later stated that these rumors were exaggerations and that production continued as normal. McGregor further stated that while filming was indeed delayed to January [[2021]], the series' intended release date would remain unaffected.{{WebCite|url=https://www.thewrap.com/obi-wan-star-ewan-mcgregor-downplays-all-this-bulls-about-disney-series-delay|text='Obi-Wan' Star Ewan McGregor Downplays 'All This Bulls—' About Disney+ Series Delay|author=Ross A. Lincoln|date=2020-01-23|work=[[Wikipedia:TheWrap|''TheWrap'']]|archivedate=20200728115204}} On [[April 2]], 2020, it was reported that [[Wikipedia:John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum|''John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum'']] writer [[Joby Harold]] was hired to write the series, replacing Amini, who left the project back in January.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/obi-wan-kenobi-disney-plus-series-joby-harold-1234569286|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi Disney Plus Series Enlists Joby Harold as New Writer (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Joe Otterson|date=2020-04-02|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200709182158}} This was confirmed in 2022, as Kennedy revealed in an interview that she was concerned with the direction of the scripts. She had shut down production in January 2020, and hired Harold to replace Amini. Despite leaving the project, Amini still received writing and story credits for four episodes of the season. [[File:Obi-Wan_Kenobi_series_logo.png|thumb|right|250px|The original series logo revealed in December 2020]] In April 2020, French press release reported that the series was scheduled to debut in 2022.{{WebCite|url=https://thedirect.com/article/disney-press-release-gives-possible-dates-for-obi-wan-and-cassian-andor-series|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi Show Given 2022 Release, Cassian Andor Series Still Set To Debut Next Year|author=Tom Drew|date=2020-04-06|work=[https://thedirect.com thedirect.com]|archivedate=20200807090106}} In September 2020, McGregor expected the show to begin filming in spring 2021.{{WebCite|url=https://www.etonline.com/ewan-mcgregor-says-obi-wan-series-will-be-a-standalone-season-exclusive-152725|text=Ewan McGregor Says 'Obi-Wan' Series Will Be a 'Standalone Season' (Exclusive)|author=Meredith B. Kile|date=2020-09-09|work=[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Tonight|''Entertainment Tonight'']]|archivedate=20200910180641}} On [[October 9]], 2020, Ewan McGregor confirmed while on [[Wikipedia:BBC|BBC's]] [[Wikipedia:The Graham Norton Show|''The Graham Norton Show'']] that filming was scheduled for [[March]] of 2021.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/ewan-mcgregor-disney-plus-obi-wan-kenobi-star-wars-1234800083|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi Disney Plus Series to Begin Filming in March, Says Ewan McGregor|author=Ellise Shafer|date=2020-10-10|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20201015142531}} On [[December 10]], 2020, more news on the series broke, including confirmation that the series would take place in [[9 BBY]] and the announcement that [[Hayden Christensen]] would reprise his role as [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] for the series. The series' logo was also revealed.{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}} ===Production=== {{Quote|There are certain cultural things that we can understand right away, and culturally specific things design-wise. Like, 'Oh, maybe we shouldn't do this, but this?' Things that, intuitively, we pick up. It's been an absolute joy working with Deb because she gets it. She's very smart and knows what she wants. I really enjoy that collaboration because now, I feel like, for the ''Obi-Wan'' series especially, we have an opportunity to bring a richness to it that hasn't been explored. And I'm working with Chung-hoon ''[Chung]'', our director of photography, he's brilliant. He has a wonderful eye.|Doug Chiang|{{SW|url=news/doug-chiang-interview|text="There is a Strength in Asian Culture": A Conversation with Lucasfilm Legend Doug Chiang}}}} On [[March 29]], 2021, Lucasfilm announced the cast list for the series, which includes [[Moses Ingram]], Joel Edgerton, [[Bonnie Maree Piesse]], [[Kumail Nanjiani]], [[Indira Varma]], [[Rupert Friend]], [[O'Shea Jackson Jr.]], [[Sung Kang]], [[Simone Kessell]], and [[Benny Safdie]]. Filming began in April. In late 2020, the series was said to be produced using "The Volume,"{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/obi-wan-ewan-mcgregor-why-excited-to-return-star-wars|text=Obi-Wan: Ewan McGregor On Why He's So Excited To Return To Star Wars|author=Ben Travis|date=2020-09-11|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (film magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20200912005133}} a technology previously used for ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''.{{DisneyGallery|Technology}} On [[May 19]], 2021, it was revealed that veteran ''Star Wars'' concept artist Doug Chiang collaborated with director Deborah Chow on the series, making heavy use of different cultures for new designs. At least six department heads are of Asian American heritage, with [[Chung-hoon Chung]] serving as the director of photography. Filming wrapped on September 19, 2021.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2021/09/ewan-mcgregor-teases-obi-wan-kenobi-series-following-emmy-win-for-halston-1234839937|text=Ewan McGregor Teases 'Obi-Wan Kenobi' Series Following Emmy Win For 'Halston': "It Will Not Disappoint"|author=Matt Grobar|date=2021-09-19|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20210919080517}} On [[February 9]], 2022, StarWars.com announced that the series would premiere [[May 25]] of that year.{{SW|url=news/obi-wan-kenobi-premiere-date|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' Will Debut May 27 on Disney+}} The first teaser trailer for the series was released on [[March 9]].{{SWYouTube|TWTfhyvzTx0|Obi-Wan Kenobi | Teaser Trailer | Disney+|sw_url=video/teaser-trailer-obi-wan-kenobi}} It was announced on [[March 31]] that the premiere for the series would be pushed back to [[May 27]], 2022, with the first two episodes premiering together.{{SW|url=news/obi-wan-kenobi-may-27|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' to Premiere May 27 with Two Episodes}} On [[February 28]], 2022, the [[Wikipedia:Writers Guild of America West|Writers Guild of America West]] revealed the final writing credits of the season, which includes the previously unannounced writers Stuart Beattie, [[Andrew Stanton]], and [[Hannah Friedman]] alongside Joby Harold and Hossein Amini. In a post-series interview with ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'', series composer [[Natalie Holt]] stated, "we didn't have very much time on ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'', as it was a very compressed process," which she stated created "challenges" for herself and Chow while working on the soundtrack. Holt had been hired as composer in December and needed to be ready for music recording by early March.{{InsiderCite|215|Parallel Lines}} ===Music=== On [[February 17]], 2022, [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] released an article announcing that composer [[John Williams]] would return to the ''Star Wars'' universe, writing the main theme for the Kenobi character within the show, but that he wouldn't be scoring the series itself.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/artisans/news/john-williams-obi-wan-kenobi-theme-star-wars-series-1235185228|text=John Williams Returns to 'Star Wars' Universe with 'Obi-Wan Kenobi' Theme (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Jon Burlingame|date=2022-02-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220319074516}} On [[April 22]] of that year, it was announced that Natalie Holt would be scoring the series, utilizing Williams' Kenobi theme. Additional music for the series was written by [[William Ross]], a longtime Williams collaborator, as well as Peter Nickals, Jon Opstad, and Max Aruj. ==Adaptations and tie-in media== On March 5, 2024, it was announced that ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' would be released on April 30, 2024 on 4K UHD and Blu-ray in SteelBook packaging. Bonus features include original box art by Attila Szarka, concept art cards, and never-before-seen featurettes.{{SW|url=news/obi-wan-kenobi-andor-4k-blu-ray|text=''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' and ''Andor'' Head to 4K Ultra HD and Blu-ray|date=2024-03-05}}{{webCite|url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/andor-moon-knight-obi-wan-kenobi-falcon-winter-soldier-4k-blu-ray-1235930078|text='Andor,' 'Moon Knight,' 'Obi-Wan Kenobi' and 'The Falcon and The Winter Soldier' to Bow on Blu-ray With Deleted Scenes, Featurettes|author=Todd Gilchrist|date=2024-04-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20240305152615}} ==Media== ===Episodes=== {|{{Prettytable}} !
